provenance: Hand-assembled, not harness output. Unlike every other file in this tree it carries no metadata or grid block, because no single harness run produced it: the repeated-passage arm's acceptance was read from engine decode-batch log lines and the non-repetitive arm's from a spec_verify_calls_total counter delta. It is covered by neither the provenance gate nor the integrity audit. benchmarks/run_realistic_sweep_kimi_k3.py exists to replace it with a file that is. Treat these numbers as a recorded observation, not an audited measurement.
purpose: Isolate the effect of prompt predictability on speculative-decoding gains, holding engine, hardware, concurrency and generated-token count constant.
hardware: 2 x a4-highgpu-8g (16 x NVIDIA B200 HGX), RoCEv2, direct container port 8000

shape.note: Probe issues exactly c requests as one burst; the Table 4 sweep issues 2c through a c-wide pool, so the probe pays more batch drain. Acceptance is unaffected by drain.

arms.name: repeated_passage_prompt
arms.acceptance_source: engine decode-batch log lines, mean over the sweep window by #running-req

finding: Accepted tokens per verify step falls from 6.29-6.41 to 2.20-2.28 (~2.8x) when prompts stop being a repeated passage, stable across c=8/16/32. Table 4's speedups are a ceiling for repetitive or highly structured traffic.
caveat: The non-speculative baseline could not be re-run on this prompt set before teardown, and these prompts are 66% longer (1523.0 / 917.625 = 1.66; an earlier revision of this file said 46%, which was wrong), so 656.60 vs the 492.02 default-profile figure is indicative, not a controlled comparison.
